## 2026-09-29 — Visual design pivot: Organization retrofitted to modals (second pass)

Continues the 2026-09-27 design pivot (see `DECISIONS.md#d-040`, `DESIGN.md`). This session: Organization's four CRUD sections converted from inline forms to the `<x-modal>` pattern, plus a real bug found and fixed in the modal component itself.

- **Bug found and fixed: the modal component's `open-modal`/`close-modal` event contract was broken for any Livewire-side close.** `$this->dispatch('close-modal', name: '...')` sends the browser event's `detail` as an *object* (`{ name: '...' }`) — the Alpine listener from the first design-pivot session compared `$event.detail` directly against a plain string, which could never match an object. Every `close-modal` dispatch from PHP was silently a no-op. Fixed by standardizing on `{ name: '...' }` for both open and close, from both Livewire and any plain JS/Alpine trigger — see `DESIGN.md`'s new "Modal open/close event contract" section. Caught while building Organization's modals (the first real Livewire-dispatched close-modal usage), not by any existing test — Blade/Alpine event wiring isn't something Pint/Larastan/Pest can see. Also fixed the one other pre-existing consumer of the modal component, `/profile`'s Delete Account confirmation (`resources/views/livewire/profile/delete-user-form.blade.php`), which was still written against the *old*, pre-rewrite Jetstream-style `<x-modal :show focusable>` API and had been silently broken since the first design-pivot session — nothing pointed it out because `/profile` isn't linked from any nav (dead Breeze scaffolding, superseded by `/my-profile`) and no test renders it interactively.
- **Regression test added per Organization component** (`DepartmentsTest`, `DutyStationsTest`, `PositionsTest`, `SalaryGradesTest`): `openCreate()` resets the form and dispatches `open-modal`; `save()`/`cancel()` dispatch `close-modal` — asserted via Livewire's `assertDispatched($name, ...$params)`. Doesn't (can't, via Pest) prove the Alpine listener actually reacts to the dispatch, but locks in that the PHP side emits the right event/name pair, which is exactly what was silently wrong before.
- **Departments/DutyStations/Positions/SalaryGrades**: each gained an `openCreate()` action (resets the form, dispatches `open-modal`) so the "Add X" button no longer needs an inline Alpine dispatch guessing at fresh state; `edit()` now also dispatches `open-modal`; `save()` and `cancel()` dispatch `close-modal`. Views: card header now has a `<x-button>` "Add X" trigger, list rows use `<x-badge variant="neutral">` for code/grade tags, and the form itself moved into `<x-modal name="...-form">` + `<x-modal-header>`.
- `composer ci`: 159 tests (up from 155 — 4 new modal-contract tests), Pint and Larastan clean.
- Verified against the live running server via the same temporary `/__demo-login/{email}` route pattern (added, used, then removed surgically — confirmed `routes/web.php`'s diff was clean afterward): `/organization` renders all four "Add X" buttons and their modal markup; `/profile`'s fixed delete-account modal renders without error.
- Updated `DESIGN.md`'s "retrofitted vs. pending" list and `00-build-plan.md`'s design-pivot note.

**Still pending, unchanged from the last entry:** Employees create/edit, Audit Log, Super Admin, Approvals demo, Notifications, PersonalDetails' dependent/contact forms.

## 2026-09-27 — Visual design pivot: retrofitting the Nova HRM reference's actual UI (first pass)

Not a build-plan step — a correction prompted by the user asking to see the running app and noticing it didn't match the Nova Humanitarian HRM reference PDF visually, even though every step since Phase 0 had followed its *functional* spec (nav/fields/workflow). The user gave a standing instruction: retrofit what exists, and every future screen must follow the provided UI from now on. See [`DECISIONS.md#d-040`](DECISIONS.md#d-040) for the full account and [`DESIGN.md`](DESIGN.md) for the extracted design tokens (new, binding reference going forward).

- Sampled ~22 representative pages from the 70-page reference PDF (Sign In, Home, My Profile's five tabs, list+modal pairs for Dependents/Leave/Timesheet/Self-Assessment/Asset Verification, Safeguarding) to extract concrete tokens rather than re-reading all 70 pages.
- Rebuilt `resources/views/components/layouts/app.blade.php`: new persistent top bar (page title + signed-in user's email as a constant subtitle, matching every reference screen — plus a notification bell), blue accents (was indigo), widened content area (`max-w-6xl`, was `max-w-3xl`).
- New reusable design-system components: `<x-button>` (near-black `slate-900` primary, matching the reference's actual CTA color — not a brand accent, confirmed across 6+ reference screens), `<x-badge>`, `<x-stat-card>`, `<x-modal>`/`<x-modal-header>` (Alpine-based, global `open-modal`/`close-modal` window events so any Livewire component can trigger one without a nested Alpine scope).
- Global indigo→blue color sweep across all 26 Blade files with color classes.
- **My Profile** rebuilt as a tabbed interface (Edit Profile | Personal Details | Employment | Documents | History), matching the reference's tab structure exactly — replacing the previous stacked-cards layout. All five Livewire components still mount on page load; Alpine `x-show` toggles which is visible.
- **Dashboard** rebuilt as a real Home screen (`App\Livewire\Dashboard\Home` + `resources/views/livewire/dashboard/home.blade.php`): blue-gradient profile header card (name/position/department/duty station/employee number), a stat-card row (pending approvals, unread notifications, document count, dependent count — all real data via `ApprovalWorkflow::awaitingActionBy`, `unreadNotifications()`, `Employee::documents()/dependents()`), and quick-action links to real existing screens only. Deliberately does **not** show Leave-balance/Payroll-style cards the reference's Home screen has — those modules don't exist yet, and fabricated numbers would be dishonest. `dashboard.blade.php` now renders `@livewire('dashboard.home')`, which itself still renders `@livewire('system-status')` internally — kept for `AuthenticationTest`'s existing `assertSeeLivewire(SystemStatus::class)` assertion.
- Same Larastan/`#[Computed]` pattern as Step 1.2 applied again: `Home::employee()` split into the `#[Computed]` wrapper plus a private `resolveEmployee()` that `documentsCount()`/`dependentsCount()` call internally instead of `$this->employee`.
- Verified against the live running server: re-seeded the dev database (`migrate:fresh --seed` — it had been emptied since the last session), used the established temporary `/__demo-login/{email}` route to get a real authenticated session (needed `User::withoutGlobalScope(TenantScope::class)` since, pre-login, no tenant context exists yet and `User` is tenant-scoped — the same `tenant-aware-eloquent` exemption `AppServiceProvider` already grants `Auth::attempt()`/session-reload, applied manually here for the same reason), confirmed the new top bar/blue accents/stat cards/tabs all render with real data and zero remaining `indigo-` references, then removed the temporary route surgically (edited the block back out, not `git checkout`) — confirmed `routes/web.php` has a clean diff afterward.
- `composer ci`: 155 tests still passing, Pint clean, Larastan clean.
- Logged [`DECISIONS.md#d-040`](DECISIONS.md#d-040), created `DESIGN.md`.

**Explicitly not done yet, tracked in `DESIGN.md`'s "still pending" list, not silently dropped:** Organization, Employees create/edit, Audit Log, Super Admin, Approvals demo, Notifications, and PersonalDetails' dependent/contact forms haven't been converted to the modal pattern yet — color sweep only for those screens so far. Next session continues the retrofit there.

## 2026-09-27 — Phase 1 Step 1.2: Employee Portal shell + profile

Continued from Step 1.1 (Employee data model). Filled in the three real tiles My Profile was still waiting on (Personal Details, Employment, History), and made a real design correction to Documents now that Employee exists.

- **Personal Details** (`App\Livewire\Employees\PersonalDetails`, new): self-service contact-info editing (phone/personal email/address) plus full dependents & emergency contacts management, including insurance beneficiary percentage allocation. "Must total 100%" is enforced as *never exceed* 100% across all of an employee's beneficiaries, checked on every save, with the running total always visible — a hard "always exactly 100% right now" rule isn't realistic for incremental data entry, and doesn't actually protect against the real risk (a payout error from over-allocation) any better. See [`DECISIONS.md#d-039`](DECISIONS.md#d-039).
- **Employment** (`App\Livewire\Employees\Employment`, new, read-only): department, position, duty station, staff category, and full contract history — including the employee's own salary grade, which is fine to show them even though salary is Restricted-tier data, because they're always exactly the record's own owner.
- **History** (`App\Livewire\Employees\History`, new): a self-scoped view of `AuditLogEntry` — the actual change-logging was already automatic (`User` and `Employee` both use `Auditable` from Step 0.8); this just makes it visible, reusing the existing engine instead of building a second one.
- **Documents moved from `User` to `Employee`** as the thing it attaches to — a real correction, not strictly required by this step's letter, made because Step 1.1 established that not every employee has a login, so a `User`-keyed document repository could never work for them. `App\Livewire\Documents\MyDocuments` became `App\Livewire\Employees\Documents`; `DocumentPolicy` updated to match. See [`DECISIONS.md#d-038`](DECISIONS.md#d-038).
- **A Larastan/Livewire interaction fixed at the pattern level:** Livewire's `#[Computed]` methods throw an exception if called directly — `$this->employee` (magic property access) is the only legal way to read one, even from the component's own action methods. Larastan doesn't see that magic outside Blade (which it doesn't scan at all), so it flagged every internal read as an undefined property. Fixed by splitting each into a thin `#[Computed]` wrapper plus a plain private `resolveX()` method action code calls instead, rather than suppressing — a pattern every future component mixing actions with computed state will need.
- `passport_number` on `Dependent` is encrypted at rest, same treatment as `national_id` (Step 1.1) — Restricted-tier personal data, per docs/03-roles-and-permissions.md's confidentiality tiers.
- Verified against the live running server, not just the 155-test suite: linked a real demo user to a real Employee+Contract via `tinker`, drove the real `/my-profile` page and confirmed all four tiles render, updated contact info and added two dependents with a real 60/40 beneficiary split (confirmed the raw `passport_number` database value contains no plaintext), uploaded a real document, and confirmed everything reflects correctly on reload — including the new Dependent changes appearing automatically on `/audit-log`.
- 155 tests total (up from 139): `tests/Feature/Hrm/{PersonalDetailsComponentTest,EmploymentComponentTest,HistoryComponentTest,EmployeesDocumentsComponentTest}.php`; removed the superseded `tests/Feature/Documents/MyDocumentsComponentTest.php`.
- Updated `docs/build/00-build-plan.md` (1.2 checked off), logged `DECISIONS.md#d-038/d-039`.

**Still not started:** Steps 1.3–1.16. Step 1.3 (Recruitment & Onboarding) is next.

## 2026-09-27 — Phase 1 Step 1.1: Employee data model

Phase 1 begins. Built the anchor HRM record and everything Step 1.1's checklist named: `employees`, `contracts`, `salary_grades`, `allowance_types`, `deduction_types`, `tax_brackets`.

- **`Employee`** is deliberately separate from `User`: `user_id` is nullable ("not every historical employee needs a login"), with its own name/contact fields independent of any linked portal account. Org-structure links (department/position/duty station) reuse Phase 0's Organization module directly; a self-referential `reports_to_id` covers reporting lines.
- **`Contract`** requires a `SalaryGrade` — renewal history is just multiple `Contract` rows per employee ordered by `start_date`, no separate renewal table.
- **`AllowanceType`/`DeductionType`/`TaxBracket`** are modeled and migrated now (Step 1.1's checklist names all three explicitly) but deliberately have no UI yet — nothing consumes them until Step 1.5 actually runs payroll, and a config screen for numbers nothing reads yet would be UI with no purpose.
- **A real screen** (`/employees`) where creating an employee **creates their first Contract in the same atomic action** — an employee with no contract would satisfy "created" but not this step's actual DoD ("an employee can be created with a contract and a salary grade"). `SalaryGrades` CRUD (same shape as Departments/Positions/DutyStations) was added to `/organization` for the same reason: a Contract needs real, UI-created grades to choose from, not seeded ones.
- **`national_id` is encrypted at rest** — the one field docs/02-architecture.md's security NFR explicitly names, not a blanket policy across every personal-data column. Used Laravel's native `encrypted` cast rather than a manual `Crypt::encryptString()` call; caught before it shipped that the column needed to be `text`, not `string` — ciphertext runs comfortably longer than the plaintext and can exceed a `varchar(255)`.
- **A deliberate scope boundary, not an oversight:** `Position.grade` (a free-text placeholder from Phase 0 Step 0.5, explicitly flagged there as "becomes a proper FK once Phase 1 builds Payroll") was left exactly as-is rather than converted to a `SalaryGrade` foreign key — Step 1.1's own checklist ties the salary grade link to Contract, not Position, and a position's structural grade label is a genuinely different concept from an individual contract's actual pay band. See [`DECISIONS.md#d-036`](DECISIONS.md#d-036).
- Verified against the live running server, not just the 139-test suite: created real Department/Position/DutyStation/SalaryGrade records and a real Employee+Contract via `tinker` (the same calls the Livewire component makes), confirmed the raw `national_id` database value contains no trace of the plaintext, and confirmed `/employees` and `/organization` correctly render everything — including the new Employee/Contract audit entries showing up on `/audit-log` automatically, for free, since both models already use `Auditable`.
- 139 tests total (up from 125): `tests/Feature/Hrm/EmployeesComponentTest.php` and `tests/Feature/Organization/SalaryGradesTest.php`.
- Updated `docs/build/00-build-plan.md` (1.1 checked off, Phase 1 marked in progress), logged `DECISIONS.md#d-036/d-037`.

**Still not started:** Steps 1.2–1.16 (the rest of HRM & Payroll). Step 1.2 (Employee Portal shell + profile) is next.

## 2026-09-27 — Phase 0 Step 0.11: Super Admin portal — Phase 0 complete

The last step of Phase 0. Continued from Step 0.10 (reporting). Built tenant CRUD, a basic cross-tenant system health view, and a logged impersonation flow — the platform layer that sits outside every tenant.

- **Tenant creation makes a tenant AND its first admin together**, not just a bare tenant row: a tenant with zero users would exist but nobody could ever log into it, which would fail Step 0.11's own DoD ("immediately usable"). The new admin gets HR Admin by default — a sensible first role for a fresh org to start configuring itself from.
- **Suspension is actually enforced**, not just a database flag: `LoginForm::authenticate()` blocks a login outright for a suspended tenant's user, even with the correct password. Known, honestly-documented limitation: login-time only, not a forced kick of already-active sessions — logged as [`QUESTIONS.md#q9`](QUESTIONS.md#q9) rather than silently left unhandled.
- **System health**: active/suspended tenant counts, total users, pending/failed (24h) queue jobs (real `jobs`/`failed_jobs` table counts, not placeholders), total document storage across every tenant (reusing Step 0.9's `documents.size`).
- **Impersonation** (`App\Support\Impersonation\ImpersonationManager`): session-based, defensively re-validated on stop (a tampered session value is rejected, not trusted — no support for nested impersonation, since it was never a real requirement), and — the more interesting design choice — every start/stop writes a real audit log entry attributed to the **target's** tenant, so it shows up on that tenant's own Audit Log screen. "Logged" means visible to the org being supported, not just to platform staff. A persistent "You're impersonating X — Stop" banner lives in the shared layout.
- **Two real bugs, both caught before or by the test suite rather than living in production:**
  1. A Super Admin genuinely has no ambient tenant at all (not "the wrong one" — `IdentifyTenant` only sets one when `$user->tenant_id` is truthy, never true for Super Admin) — so `Auditable`'s automatic logging had nothing to fill `tenant_id` from when a Super Admin action triggered it, throwing a `NOT NULL constraint failed` on every write. Same root cause as D-031 (ambient test-context masking a real gap) — caught by verifying against the real database via `tinker`, not just the in-memory test DB. Fixed with a subject-derived fallback on `AuditLogEntry`. See [`DECISIONS.md#d-033`](DECISIONS.md#d-033).
  2. The impersonation banner's Blade view had no root HTML element when idle (the common case) — since it lives in the *global* layout, this would have 500'd every single page in the app. Caught immediately by the very first `composer ci` run after wiring it in (every page-rendering test failed at once with the same stack trace), not by clicking a broken page live. See [`DECISIONS.md#d-034`](DECISIONS.md#d-034).
- Verified against the live running server end to end, not just the 125-test suite: created a real tenant+admin via `tinker`, confirmed the real audit trail attributed it correctly (proving the D-033 fix against real persistent data), logged in as the new admin over a real HTTP session (organization: 200, super-admin: 403), suspended and reactivated the tenant while reproducing `LoginForm`'s exact suspension check against real data, and ran a full real impersonation cycle confirming the resulting audit entries render correctly on the target tenant's own Audit Log page.
- 125 tests total (up from 108): `tests/Feature/SuperAdmin/{TenantManagementTest,ImpersonationTest}.php`.
- Updated `docs/build/00-build-plan.md` (0.11 checked off, Phase 0 marked complete), logged `DECISIONS.md#d-033/d-034/d-035`, logged `QUESTIONS.md#q9`.

**Phase 0 is complete.** Steps 0.1 through 0.11 are all done, live-verified, and tested. Phase 1 (the first real module — HRM) is next; see `docs/build/00-build-plan.md`'s Phase 1 section and `docs/04-module-hrm.md` for the real spec.

## 2026-09-27 — Phase 0 Step 0.10: reporting & export framework

Continued from Step 0.9 (document store). Built the shared Excel/CSV/PDF export framework every module's future "Reports" screen will use, and wired it into a real, already-existing screen (the Audit Log) rather than a new throwaway demo page.

- **`maatwebsite/excel`** (Excel + CSV) and **`barryvdh/laravel-dompdf`** (PDF) installed. `App\Support\Reporting\ReportDataset` is the one format-agnostic shape every format consumes (title, ordered columns, flattened rows); `App\Exports\GenericExport` (one class, shared across every future module) handles Excel+CSV; `resources/views/exports/generic-table.blade.php` (one shared layout) handles PDF. `App\Support\Reporting\ReportExporter::toExcel()/toCsv()/toPdf()` is the actual entry point — see [`DECISIONS.md#d-032`](DECISIONS.md#d-032) for why PDF goes through a hand-written Blade view rather than PhpSpreadsheet's own PDF writer bridge.
- **A real bug caught by reading framework source before wiring anything up, not by a dead button:** DomPDF's own `->download()` returns a plain `Illuminate\Http\Response`, not a `StreamedResponse`/`BinaryFileResponse` — the two types Livewire's file-download support actually recognizes. Calling it directly from a Livewire action would have silently done nothing when clicked (no error at all). Fixed by building the PDF response manually around DomPDF's raw output bytes, reusing the same `response()->streamDownload()` pattern already proven in Step 0.9's document download controller.
- **Wired into the real Audit Log screen**, not a new demo page: "Export: Excel / CSV / PDF" buttons that respect whatever event filter is active. An early version only exported who/what/when (event type, record, causer) — realized mid-step that a real audit-log export missing the actual old→new diff would be materially less useful than the on-screen expandable table it's exported from, so added a flattened "Changes" column matching the screen's own diff logic before calling this done.
- **Verified two ways:** automated tests parse the generated files back for real (PhpSpreadsheet reads the XLSX cell-by-cell, plain `str_getcsv` for CSV, a rendered-view content check plus a `%PDF-` magic-byte check for PDF) rather than just asserting "no exception thrown"; and, live against the real environment (not `Storage::fake()`), generated all three formats via `tinker` and independently confirmed them with PhpSpreadsheet and the system's own `pdfinfo`/`pdftotext` utilities — a real 1-page PDF with the correct extracted title, heading, and row text.
- 108 tests total (up from 100): `tests/Feature/Reporting/ReportExporterTest.php` and `tests/Feature/AuditLog/ExportTest.php`.
- Updated `docs/build/00-build-plan.md` (0.10 checked off), logged `DECISIONS.md#d-032`.

**Still not started:** Phase 0 Step 0.11 (Super Admin portal) — the last step before Phase 0's exit criteria are checked as a whole.

## 2026-09-27 — Phase 0 Step 0.9: document store

Continued from Step 0.8 (audit log). Built the generic document/attachment primitive: storage disk config, the `Document` model, `App\Support\Documents\DocumentStore`, a `DocumentPolicy`, and a real screen — plus found and fixed what's probably the most significant bug in Phase 0 so far, entirely through live testing.

- **Storage:** a `filesystems.documents_disk` config key indirects to `local` in dev, swappable to `s3` via `DOCUMENTS_DISK` in staging/prod with no code change — matching D-010's original plan. Never the `public` disk; documents are access-controlled, not publicly served.
- **`App\Models\Document`:** polymorphic (`documentable`), free-form `category` (categories differ per module — ID/contract/certificate for HR, evidence for Safeguarding, receipts for Procurement — so this stays a plain string, not an enum), `expiry_date`, `is_verified`/`verified_by_id`/`verified_at`, tenant- *and* path-scoped (`documents/{tenant_id}/{uuid}` on disk, independent of the DB-level scoping).
- **Encryption, actually verified, not just configured:** rather than resting the "encrypted at rest" requirement entirely on S3 server-side encryption (which can't be verified here — no real AWS credentials exist in this environment), `DocumentStore` encrypts file bytes with Laravel's `Crypt` facade *before* they ever touch any disk, local or cloud. Confirmed against the real local disk via `tinker`: the on-disk file is a base64 JSON envelope, no trace of the plaintext marker written into the source file. S3 SSE is additionally configured as defense-in-depth for real deployment, honestly logged as configured-not-verified. See [`DECISIONS.md#d-030`](DECISIONS.md#d-030).
- **A real screen, using a real record this time:** "Documents" on My Profile (`App\Livewire\Documents\MyDocuments`) — upload/list/download your own personnel documents, promoted from its own "Coming in Phase 1" placeholder. Unlike prior demo screens, `Document` attaches to the actual `User` model, matching Phase 1's real future Employee Records feature directly rather than a throwaway entity.
- **Authorization:** `App\Policies\DocumentPolicy` — the owner, the employee the document belongs to, or anyone with `HrmOrgView`. The first real use of the "record owner OR org-level permission" pattern `AuthorizationServiceProvider`'s docblock had already anticipated back in Step 0.4 for exactly this kind of Restricted-tier data.
- **The most significant bug caught in Phase 0 so far:** `IdentifyTenant` middleware ran *after* Laravel's `SubstituteBindings` — so the very first route in the whole app to use implicit route-model binding on a tenant-scoped model (`Document $document` in `/documents/{document}/download`) resolved with no tenant context yet, and `TenantScope`'s fail-closed design turned it into a 404 for everyone, including the document's own owner. This had been latent since Step 0.3 and was invisible to the entire 100-test suite, because `tests/Pest.php`'s own global `beforeEach` sets `TenantContext` directly before every test's simulated request — completely masking whether the *real* middleware pipeline could derive it correctly on its own. Found by manually driving the live server (an unexplained 404 downloading your own file), diagnosed by ruling out a stale process, confirming the route and model both worked fine outside the HTTP layer via `tinker`, then reading Laravel's actual `$middlewarePriority` source to understand why an appended-but-unprioritized middleware stays wherever it was appended. Fixed with `$middleware->prependToPriorityList()`. Added a dedicated regression test that deliberately clears `TenantContext` and relies entirely on the real middleware chain — confirmed it genuinely fails without the fix (temporarily reverted `bootstrap/app.php` via `git stash` to check) before trusting it. See [`DECISIONS.md#d-031`](DECISIONS.md#d-031).
- Verified against the live running server end to end: uploaded a real file as `employee@demo.test`, confirmed the raw on-disk bytes are ciphertext, downloaded it successfully as the owner, got 403 as a different employee, 200 as `hr-admin@demo.test`, and 404 for an HR Admin belonging to an entirely different tenant (created on the fly for this check).
- 100 tests total (up from 87): `tests/Feature/Documents/{DocumentStoreTest,MyDocumentsComponentTest,DownloadAccessTest}.php` and `tests/Feature/Tenancy/IdentifyTenantMiddlewareOrderTest.php`.
- Updated `docs/build/00-build-plan.md` (0.9 checked off), confirmed `D-010`'s tentative status, logged `DECISIONS.md#d-030` and `#d-031`.

**Still not started:** Phase 0 Steps 0.10–0.11 (reporting & export framework, Super Admin portal). Step 0.10 is next.

## 2026-09-26 — Phase 0 Step 0.8: audit log

Continued straight from Step 0.7 (notifications). Installed `spatie/laravel-activitylog` as anticipated back in D-005, and wired it into every tenant-scoped model.

- **Tenant isolation for the audit trail itself, not just the models it watches:** the package's stock `activity_log` table has no tenant column — every organization's audit trail would otherwise sit in one shared, unscoped table, violating this codebase's own standing rule. Added `tenant_id` directly to the published migration and introduced `App\Models\AuditLogEntry` (extends the package's own `Activity`, adds `BelongsToTenant`, registered as `activitylog.activity_model`) so every logged row is tenant-scoped like everything else.
- **A design trap caught before it was ever run, not after:** the obvious-looking shortcut was to put `LogsActivity` directly inside `BelongsToTenant`, since audit logging should apply to every tenant-scoped model anyway. But `AuditLogEntry` itself needs `BelongsToTenant` for its own tenant scoping — folding `LogsActivity` in there too would make every audit log row's creation try to log itself, recursively, forever. Caught by tracing the trait composition on paper before writing the code, not by hitting a stack overflow at runtime. Solved with a separate `App\Models\Concerns\Auditable` trait (composing `LogsActivity` + default `LogOptions`: log all fillable attributes, only when dirty, skip empty logs, exclude `tenant_id` from the diff since it's redundant with the log row's own column) applied alongside `BelongsToTenant` on every actual business model — never on `AuditLogEntry`. See [`DECISIONS.md#d-029`](DECISIONS.md#d-029).
- Applied `Auditable` to all nine tenant-scoped models: `User` (with `password` additionally excluded from the diff, even hashed — no legitimate reason for a hash to sit in an audit trail), `Department`, `DutyStation`, `Position`, `ApprovalChain`, `ApprovalChainStep`, `ApprovalInstance`, `ApprovalInstanceStep`, `TestRequest`.
- Causer resolution needed zero extra wiring — the package's `ActivityLogger` already defaults to `Auth::user()` on the active guard, confirmed by reading its `CauserResolver` source rather than assuming, then verified live via `tinker`.
- **A real screen, not just rows in a table:** `/audit-log` (`App\Livewire\AuditLog\Index`) — paginated, filterable by event type, each entry showing who did what to which record with an expandable old→new field diff (booleans/nulls rendered as words, not blank cells, so a `false→true` flip on something like `is_active` doesn't look like nothing happened). Linked in the sidebar's "Administration" section next to Organization, gated by `Permission::HrmOrgView` — no dedicated audit-log permission exists yet, logged as [`QUESTIONS.md#q8`](QUESTIONS.md#q8) rather than guessed at silently.

## 2026-09-26 — Phase 0 Step 0.7: notification engine

Continued straight from Step 0.6 (approval engine). User said "Fix and continue" after a session gap; a QA sweep found nothing actually broken (a zsh word-splitting bug in the sweep script itself briefly made the server look down — false alarm, documented, fixed). With CI clean and nothing outstanding, moved on to Step 0.7 exactly as scoped: wire notifications onto the two events the approval engine already dispatches, without touching the engine itself.

- **One new event, added deliberately at this step, not before:** `ApprovalInstanceSubmitted`, dispatched at the end of `ApprovalWorkflow::submit()`. Needed because the existing `ApprovalStepActedOn`/`ApprovalInstanceFinished` events only fire once someone *acts* — step 1's approver would never be notified of a brand-new submission without this.
- **Two listeners** in `app/Listeners/Approvals/`: `NotifyEligibleApprovers` (fires on submission and on any non-final approval — notifies whoever holds the *new* current step's role) and `NotifyRequesterOfDecision` (fires on every step decision — tells the requester what happened, whether that's "moved to the next step," "fully approved," or "rejected"). Both synchronous (not `ShouldQueue`) since there's no queue worker running in this environment yet — documented as a thing to revisit once there is one.
- **Two notification classes** (`App\Notifications\Approvals\ApprovalNeeded`, `ApprovalDecisionMade`), each rendering both a `database` and `mail` channel. A new `App\Support\Notifications\NotificationType` enum catalogs all five notification types the platform will eventually need (approval needed/decision have real triggers now; document/contract-expiring and budget-threshold are seeded as documented placeholders for modules that don't exist yet) — same "typed enum catalog" pattern already used for roles and permissions.
- **First "coming soon" placeholder promoted to a real screen:** `/notifications` (`App\Livewire\Notifications\Inbox`) — paginated inbox, mark-one-read, mark-all-read, and an unread-count badge on the sidebar nav item (`resources/views/components/layouts/app.blade.php`).
- **Two real bugs found, one by the CI loop and one by re-reading Laravel's own source before writing code:**
  1. `bootstrap/app.php` never called `->withEvents()` — Laravel's event auto-discovery (`handle*()` methods in `app/Listeners`, matched by type-hinted event parameter) is opt-in, not on by default, contrary to what the "no listener yet" comments left in Step 0.6's event classes implicitly assumed. Caught by tracing the framework source before assuming discovery would just work; verified with `php artisan event:list`. See [`DECISIONS.md#d-027`](DECISIONS.md#d-027).
  2. `NotifyEligibleApprovers` imported `Illuminate\Notifications\Notification` (the base class every notification extends) instead of `Illuminate\Support\Facades\Notification` (the facade with a static `send()`) — a fatal error at runtime. Larastan flagged it immediately (`staticMethod.notFound`) in the same `composer ci` run it was written in, and a Pest test failed with the real `Error` independently. Distinguished this from prior genuine Larastan false positives (D-016, D-026) by verifying via `tinker` that the *correct* class does have the method the code was trying to call — confirming this one was a real bug, not a static-analysis gap. See [`DECISIONS.md#d-028`](DECISIONS.md#d-028).
- **Verified against the live running server, not just tests:** started `php artisan serve`, logged in as the seeded `employee@demo.test` via a temporary local-only route (added and then surgically removed afterward, per the established practice), and drove the exact same `ApprovalWorkflow` methods the UI calls via `tinker` (submit → supervisor approves → HR Admin approves). Confirmed a real `notifications` table row landed with the right message, `storage/logs/laravel.log` contains a fully-rendered email with the correct subject and body, `GET /notifications` renders both real notification messages with the correct unread count, and the sidebar badge on `/dashboard` shows the right number.
- 78 tests total (up from 69): `tests/Feature/Notifications/ApprovalNotificationsTest.php` (submission/approval/rejection notify the right people and nobody else, plus one test that skips `Notification::fake()` entirely to prove a real database row is persisted, not just that Laravel *would* have sent something) and `tests/Feature/Notifications/InboxComponentTest.php` (a user sees only their own notifications, can mark one or all as read). Also had to fix an existing test (`EmployeePortalShellTest`) that still expected `/notifications` to be a "coming in Phase 1" placeholder now that it's a real screen — same class of thing as D-024's nav promotions.

- **The engine itself:** `App\Support\Approvals\ApprovalWorkflow` — `submit()`, `approve()`, `reject()`, `canAct()`, `awaitingActionBy()`. Segregation of duties enforced structurally in `canAct()`: the requester is denied even if they hold the current step's role, not left to callers to remember. Rejecting marks remaining steps `Skipped`, not left looking pending. Domain events (`ApprovalStepActedOn`, `ApprovalInstanceFinished`) dispatched on every decision — no listener yet, Step 0.7 attaches one without touching this code again.

- **Larastan false positive, handled the same way as before (D-016):** it infers `$instance->status` as a plain `string` rather than the `ApprovalStatus` enum declared in `casts()` — doesn't yet understand enum casts declared via the newer method-based `casts(): array` syntax. Verified empirically via `tinker` that the cast genuinely works at runtime before adding a scoped, documented `ignoreErrors` entry (not an inline suppress-comment).
- **Bug #1 — a systemic gap, not a typo:** `tenant_id` wasn't in the `#[Fillable(...)]` list of any tenant-scoped model built since Step 0.4 except `User`. Invisible until `DemoTenantSeeder` (which runs under `WithoutModelEvents`, so the auto-fill hook never fires) tried to set it explicitly and got a `NOT NULL constraint failed`. Fixed across all 8 affected models (Department, DutyStation, Position, and all four approval tables) — now a standing rule for every future tenant-scoped model, logged as D-025, with a regression test proving explicit `tenant_id` assignment actually works.
- **Bug #2 — caught only by manually driving the real app, not by the test suite:** the Livewire `Demo::submit()` method never set `requester_id` at all. Every test in the first-pass `ApprovalWorkflowTest.php` used `TestRequest::factory()` (which sets `requester_id` itself), so the actual bug in the actual UI entry point was invisible to a fully-green test suite. Found by driving the real page via `tinker` before calling the step done, per the "verify against the live server" habit from previous sessions. Fixed, and — more importantly — added `tests/Feature/Approvals/DemoComponentTest.php` testing the real `Livewire::test(Demo::class)` entry point end to end, not just the service underneath it. Logged as D-026 with the general lesson spelled out: testing a service isn't the same as testing the UI code that's supposed to call it.

Merged deliberately rather than accepting either side wholesale: deleted Breeze's duplicate top-nav layout and its unused public "welcome" page (no self-serve signup exists — D-018), kept and enhanced the sidebar shell from Step 0.2 (added signed-in-user info + logout), pointed `dashboard.blade.php`/`profile.blade.php` at it, and restored the Step 0.3 Pest customizations Breeze had reset.
- **Removed `/register` entirely** — route, Volt page, and its generated test — rather than leaving an unrouted or (worse) silently-live self-signup path sitting in the codebase. Logged as D-018: accounts come from HR Admin or Super Admin, always with a tenant already known.
- **Solved the login-time tenant resolution problem flagged (and deliberately deferred) in Step 0.3 (D-015).** It turned out to be sharper than originally scoped: it's not just the login query that has to bypass `TenantScope` — Laravel reloads the user from the session on *every single request* via the same guard/provider path, so without the fix, a user would appear logged out again on the very next page load. Fixed with a custom `tenant-aware-eloquent` auth provider (`EloquentUserProvider::withQuery()` + a named provider driver registered in `AppServiceProvider::boot()`) rather than subclassing the provider — Laravel already exposes exactly this extension point.
- **Installed `spatie/laravel-permission`, deliberately without its "teams" feature.** Reasoned through why it isn't needed here — role assignment is already unambiguous because the `User` it's assigned to is itself tenant-scoped, and this platform's design (D-015's docblock note) already rules out one person holding different roles in two different tenants. Logged as D-019, including the trade-off (global role/permission catalog for now, not yet per-tenant-customizable — noted as a Phase 5+ evolution if ever needed, not a gap).
- Added `App\Support\Authorization\Role` and `Permission` as typed PHP enums (10 roles, 27 permissions), and `database/seeders/RolesAndPermissionsSeeder.php` assigning permissions to roles by transcribing `docs/03-roles-and-permissions.md`'s access matrix — global catalog, not per-tenant, seeded once.
- **Found and fixed a real bug while seeding demo data, not a hypothetical one:** a Super Admin account seeded with an explicit `tenant_id: null` kept coming out with the *previous* tenant's id instead. Root cause: `BelongsToTenant`'s auto-fill used `empty($model->tenant_id)`, which is `true` for both "never mentioned" and "explicitly null" — so an ambient tenant context silently overwrote the intentional null. Fixed with `array_key_exists()` instead, added a regression test for this exact scenario (not just a generic re-run), and logged as D-020, including the general lesson (`empty()`/`is_null()` are the wrong tool whenever "unset" and "set to a falsy value" are meaningfully different states).
- Built confidentiality-tier Gates (`App\Providers\AuthorizationServiceProvider`) for Safeguarding — the one domain that concretely has all three tiers (Standard/Restricted/Highly-Restricted) today. Deliberately didn't build a generic cross-module abstraction with no real consumer yet; noted the same pattern extends to other Restricted-tier data once those models exist.
- `database/seeders/DemoTenantSeeder.php` — one demo tenant, one login per role (9 tenant users + 1 Super Admin), idempotent, clearly marked local-exploration-only. README updated with the credentials and a `--seed` step.
- Implemented `MustVerifyEmail` on `User` — found Breeze's scaffolding (verify-email routes, controller, the `verified` middleware already on `/dashboard`) assumed it, but Laravel's stub model ships it commented out. Fixing this surfaced as a real Larastan error, not a guess.

## 2026-09-25 — Phase 0 Step 0.3: multi-tenancy foundation

User said "continue" to proceed to the next step. This is the step the build plan itself flags as the most architecturally significant part of Phase 0, so it got a full session on its own.

- **`tenants` table + `Tenant` model.** Org profile fields per `docs/02-architecture.md` (name, slug, logo, countries of operation as JSON, default currency, timezone, fiscal year start month), `is_active` for Super Admin suspend, plus soft deletes so offboarding a tenant never silently destroys its audit trail. Auto-generates a slug from the name on create. `TenantFactory` added for testing.
- **`BelongsToTenant` trait + `TenantScope`** (`app/Models/Concerns/BelongsToTenant.php`, `app/Models/Scopes/TenantScope.php`): applies a global Eloquent scope filtering every query to the current tenant, and auto-fills `tenant_id` on create from the current context if not already set explicitly. Applied to `User` — the real, permanent model, not a throwaway demo entity, since "every login belongs to exactly one tenant" is already the documented design.
- **Key design decision: the scope fails closed.** With no tenant context set, a tenant-scoped query returns zero rows rather than every tenant's rows — a missing context becomes a visibly broken feature instead of a silent data leak. Logged as `DECISIONS.md` D-014, along with the consequence for the `users.tenant_id` column (nullable, `restrictOnDelete()`).
- **Found and explicitly deferred a real problem, rather than papering over it:** the auth guard's future login-time credential lookup runs *before* any tenant is known (that's how tenant gets known), so it can't be tenant-scoped like everything else — it must explicitly bypass `TenantScope` and look up by a globally-unique email. Not solved now (no login flow exists yet); documented in `User`'s class docblock and logged as `DECISIONS.md` D-015, with Step 0.4 in the build plan updated to call it out as its first real task so it doesn't get silently missed later.
- **`TenantContext`** (`app/Support/Tenancy/TenantContext.php`): the current-tenant singleton, bound in `AppServiceProvider`. **`IdentifyTenant`** middleware reads it from the authenticated user post-auth and sets it for the rest of the request — appended to the `web` middleware group. Currently a no-op in practice (no login flow yet) but wired and ready for Step 0.4.
- **Tenant-aware queues:** `SetsTenantContext` job middleware + `TenantAware` trait jobs opt into (not automatic for every job — a job explicitly declares it's tenant-scoped). Proven with a test-only job class defined inline in `tests/Feature/Tenancy/TenantAwareQueueTest.php` rather than adding throwaway code to `app/Jobs` (no real job needs this until Phase 1's payroll runs). Logged as D-016, including the resulting Larastan false-positive ("trait used zero times") and how it was suppressed — a scoped, commented `ignoreErrors` entry in `phpstan.neon`, not an inline suppress-comment, with a note to remove it once a real job uses the trait.
- **The flagship test:** `tests/Feature/Tenancy/TenantIsolationTest.php` — 5 tests proving two tenants' `User` records are mutually invisible, auto-fill-on-create works, an explicit `tenant_id` isn't overridden by context, the fail-closed behavior holds with no context, and the deliberate `withoutGlobalScope` bypass works for legitimate cross-tenant admin queries. Runs in CI on every push from now on.
- Enabled `RefreshDatabase` for feature tests (`tests/Pest.php`) — needed now that migrations matter for what's being tested, wasn't needed for the Step 0.1/0.2 smoke tests.
- Verified migrations are reversible: rolled back and re-applied both new migrations before committing.
- 10 tests total, Pint and Larastan (level 5) both clean — `composer ci` passes.
- Updated `docs/build/00-build-plan.md` (0.3 checked off, 0.4 updated with the login-tenant-resolution dependency), `DECISIONS.md` (D-014, D-015, D-016), this changelog.

**Still not started:** Phase 0 Steps 0.4–0.11 (auth & RBAC — including finishing the login-time tenant resolution flagged above — org structure CRUD, approval engine, notifications, audit log, document store, reporting export, Super Admin portal). **Q5** (git workflow: direct-to-`main` vs. branches/PRs) is still open and hasn't blocked anything, but is worth answering soon now that real, security-relevant code (tenant isolation) is landing.

- Found that Laravel's default scaffold now ships `CLAUDE.md`/`AGENTS.md` files instructing an AI agent to auto-install `laravel/boost` (Laravel's official first-party AI-agent tooling). **Deliberately did not auto-run that instruction** — not part of the documented build plan, and `artisan boost:install` may prompt interactively. Replaced both files with real project-specific guidance pointing at `docs/`, noting the Boost option explicitly for later if wanted.
- **Step 0.2 (frontend stack) — done.** Confirmed Livewire + Blade + Tailwind CSS (user approved the default; [`QUESTIONS.md#q1`](QUESTIONS.md#q1) resolved). Tailwind v4 was already wired into the Laravel 13 skeleton's `package.json`/`vite.config.js`; installed `livewire/livewire` (resolved to 4.4) via Composer.
- Found Livewire 4's `make:livewire` now defaults to a new single-file-component style. Deliberately used `--class` instead to keep the classic separate PHP-class + Blade-view structure — logged as [`DECISIONS.md#d-013`](DECISIONS.md#d-013), reasoning: better fit for an app whose components carry real business logic, easier to unit-test, more familiar structure.
- Built `resources/views/components/layouts/app.blade.php` — the shared portal shell (sidebar + content, mobile-responsive, stacks below `md`), and `app/Livewire/SystemStatus.php` (+ its Blade view) as the first real component: shows Laravel/PHP version, environment, server time, and a `wire:click`-driven refresh counter, proving Livewire interactivity (not just static render) end to end. Replaced the stock Laravel welcome page with this as the new home route (`/`).
- Added `tests/Feature/SystemStatusTest.php` (initial render + the refresh interaction via `Livewire::test()`) and updated `tests/Feature/ExampleTest.php` to assert the dashboard renders and mounts the Livewire component. `composer ci` — 4 tests, Pint, and Larastan all pass.
- Updated `docs/build/00-build-plan.md`: Steps 0.1 and 0.2 checked off with dated notes on what was actually built and where it deviated from plan; Phase 0 marked in-progress.
- Updated `docs/build/QUESTIONS.md`: Q1, Q4, and Q6 moved to Resolved (Q4's answer — SQLite, not Sail — differs from what was originally proposed as the default, called out explicitly rather than quietly swapped in).
- Logged `DECISIONS.md#d-012` (SQLite for local dev, not Sail) and `#d-013` (class-based Livewire components, not Livewire 4 SFCs).
- Cleaned up: removed the temp scaffold directory, stray `.DS_Store` files, verified `.env`, `vendor/`, `node_modules/`, and `database.sqlite` are all correctly gitignored (not staged) before committing.

**Still not started:** Phase 0 Steps 0.3–0.11 (multi-tenancy foundation, auth & RBAC, org structure, approval engine, notifications, audit log, document store, reporting export, Super Admin portal). Step 0.3 (multi-tenancy) is next and is the most architecturally significant step in Phase 0 — deserves its own focused session per the build plan's own "one step, one focused session" guidance, rather than being rushed in alongside 0.1/0.2.

- Created `docs/build/` with four living documents: this changelog, [`DECISIONS.md`](DECISIONS.md), [`QUESTIONS.md`](QUESTIONS.md), and [`00-build-plan.md`](00-build-plan.md) — the task-level execution checklist derived from `09-roadmap.md`.

- Logged 7 open questions (Q1–Q7) that block or affect near-term build steps, each with the default we're proceeding under.
- **Working agreement established:** every session appends to this changelog, logs new assumptions in `DECISIONS.md` as they're made, and logs open questions in `QUESTIONS.md` instead of silently guessing on anything the user would plausibly want to weigh in on.
